result.topic_en: Euler integrates the third-order differential equation arising from a variational problem by multiplying by q dx = dp, obtaining a first integral Z - Qq = Ap + B, and from it expressions for dx and dy in terms of p that construct the curve.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 69
eius integrale ſtatim praebet
$P-\frac{dQ}{dx}=A,$
quae adhuc eſt differentialis tertii gradus.

54. Verum haec aequatio adhuc in genere integrari poteſt, multiplicetur enim per $q\,dx=dp$, vt habeatur haec aequatio
$P\,dp-q\,dQ=A\,dq$, quum vero ſit $dZ=P\,dp+Q\,dq$
erit $P\,dp=dZ-Q\,dq$, quo valore ſubſtituto aequatio reſultat haec: $dZ-Q\,dq-q\,dQ=A\,dp$, cuius integrale manifeſto eſt $Z-Qq=Ap+B$, nunc igitur pro $Z$ et $Q$ valores ſupra dati ſubſtituantur atque nanciſcemur ſequentem aequationem:
$\frac{-qq}{(1+pp)^{5:2}}=Ap+B$
mutatis igitur ſignis conſtantium colligemus
$qq=(Ap+B)(1+pp)^{5:2}$ ideoque
$q=(1+pp)^{5:4}\sqrt{(Ap+B)}=\frac{dp}{dx}$,
ſicque concludimus
$dx=\frac{dp}{(1+pp)^{\frac{5}{4}}\sqrt{(Ap+B)}}$,
hincque porro
$dy=\frac{p\,dp}{(1+pp)^{\frac{5}{4}}\sqrt{(Ap+B)}}$
quibus duabus aequationibus conſtructio curuae abſoluitur.
I 3 55.

items.quote: Verum haec aequatio adhuc in genere integrari poteſt
items.english: But this equation can still be integrated in general.

items.quote: quibus duabus aequationibus conſtructio curuae abſoluitur.
items.english: By these two equations the construction of the curve is completed.
